{{Quote|You can't take on a Star Destroyer in a fighter. Stick to something five or ten times your own size.|Puck Naeco, to Samuel Raider|<ref name="XW:OSG" />}}
'''Puck Naeco''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] from [[Denon/Legends|Denon]] who served as a [[Captain/Legends|captain]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Naeco transferred to [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]] on the [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser]] [[Independence/Legends|''Independence'']] where he helped [[Ambush in the Cron Drift|defend]] the dispersal of captured [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[communications satellite]]s near the [[Cron Drift/Legends|Cron Drift]], leading to the interception of [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] to the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. When the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] attacked the [[Great Temple/Legends|Rebel base]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], Naeco was one of several ''Independence'' pilots sent to help assist in its defense. Naeco flew as [[Red Twelve/Legends|Red Twelve]] during the battle and covered [[Red Leader/Legends|Red Leader]] [[Garven Dreis/Legends|Garven Dreis]] on his failed trench run alongside [[Red Ten/Legends|Red Ten]], [[Theron Nett/Legends|Theron Nett]]. Naeco was [[Death/Legends|killed]] when his [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]] was destroyed by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] in his [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]].

==Biography==
===Red Squadron===
{{Quote|My last mission, I caught a TIE with a fantastic shot. I'd slowed down to blast a TIE Bomber, and this TIE fighter comes up behind me too fast. I caught him coming on the rear sensor, and just pushed my nose down a little. Then, as he came over me, I raised the nose and squirted a laser blast. He went nova on one hit. It was a beautiful deflection.|Puck Naeco|<ref name="XW:OSG" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="ANH" /> [[Gender/Legends|male]] native of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Denon/Legends|Denon]]<ref name="TEGW" /> in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Puck Naeco joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] as a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] during the early [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] and,<ref name="XW:OSG" /> by [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]],<ref name="1BBY">''[[X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide]]'' begins after the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]] entered service with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], which ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' places in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]]. ''X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide'' establishes that the [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|capture of Leia Organa]] occurs at the end of [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]{{'s}} second tour of duty. Organa's capture takes place on 35:3:3 under the [[Great ReSynchronization]] dating system, placing it at the beginning of [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] according to [[Template:YearMathGRS|the following explanation]]. Events in ''X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide'' before the end of the second tour of duty therefore take place in 1 BBY.</ref> was a [[Captain/Legends|captain]] in the [[Alliance Starfighter Corps/Legends|Alliance Starfighter Corps]] and a combat veteran. Shortly after the end of [[Operation Strike Fear]], a major [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] offensive against the fledgling Rebellion, Naeco transferred to [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]] aboard the [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser]] [[Independence/Legends|''Independence'']]. Soon after arriving, Naeco joined several of his [[Squadron/Legends|squadmates]], including [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Hamo Blastwell]], Captains [[Keyan Farlander/Legends|Keyan Farlander]] and [[Samuel Raider]], [[Sunnar Jan-lo]] and [[Speedy]] in the pilots' ready room, where they discussed their combat experiences and preferred targets.<ref name="XW:OSG" /> Naeco served as a mentor to some of the younger pilots, including Farlander, [[Milar Travis]] and [[Fin Danglot]]<ref name="TEGW" /> and became known on the ''Independence'' for his practical jokes.<ref name="XW:OSG" />

[[File:NaecoCronDrift-XW.png|thumb|left|200px|Naeco's X-wing chases an Assault Gunboat in the Cron Drift.]]
Shortly before Naeco joined Red Squadron, the Alliance learned of a secret Imperial military construction project. In an effort to uncover the nature of the project, [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] devised a plan to tap into the Empire's communication network, and a [[Battle of Orron III|previous operation]] had captured a shipment of Imperial [[communications satellite]]s. The [[Satellite/Legends|satellites]] were to replace several Imperial satellites near a Rebel [[AX-235|listening post]] in the [[Cron Drift/Legends|Cron Drift]] [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid field]].<ref name="XW">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref> Naeco was assigned as Farlander's [[Wingmate/Legends|wingmate]] in a pair of [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighters]] to protect the transfer of the stolen satellites from the [[BFF-1 bulk freighter/Legends|BFF-1 bulk freighter]] ''[[Ojai]]'' to the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[Jeffrey]]'' in the Cron Drift. Less than a [[Standard minute/Legends|minute]] after the Rebels arrived, they were [[Ambush in the Cron Drift|attacked]] by several Imperial [[Alpha-class Xg-1 Star Wing/Legends|Assault Gunboats]] and four [[Delta-class DX-9 stormtrooper transport|''Delta''-class DX-9 stormtrooper transports]]. The two pilots [[Starfighter combat/Legends|engaged]] the new arrivals, with Farlander leaving Naeco to fight the Assault Gunboats while he destroyed the [[Transport/Legends|transports]], until the Rebel [[Starship/Legends|ships]] completed the transfer.<ref name="XW:OSG" /> The ''Jeffrey'' later deployed the captured satellites, allowing the Alliance to intercept [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] to the Empire's new weapon, the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]].<ref name="XW" />

When the other pilots became aware that Naeco was attracted to Jan-lo, several of them devised a scheme to get their revenge for his numerous practical jokes. Jan-lo indicated that she was interested in Naeco and told him to meet her in a storage area of the ship's [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] section. Following Farlander's advice not to waste any [[Time/Legends|time]], Naeco walked into the dark room, straight over to who he thought was Jan-lo and kissed her, only to discover when the others turned the lights on that he was kissing a Quarren member of the kitchen staff. Though he laughed the incident off, Naeco cut down on the practical jokes afterward. Jan-lo was later injured during an [[Battle of the Circarpous system (Galactic Civil War)|attack]] on the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Intrepid (Imperial I-class)|''Intrepid'']], and Naeco was among the pilots who visited her while she underwent [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] therapy.<ref name="XW:OSG" />

In early [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="0BBY">''[[X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide]]'' establishes that the events of [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]{{'s}} third tour of duty take place between the [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|capture of Leia Organa]] and the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Both of these events occur in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> Naeco, Farlander and Raider witnessed the arrival of the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Privateer/Legends|privateer]] and [[Merchant/Legends|trader]] [[Tuz]] aboard the ''Independence'' when he made a [[Capture of the Sidral II|delivery]] of stolen Imperial equipment. Curious about the visitor, Naeco invited Tuz and his entourage to join the Rebels for a drink in the pilots' lounge. When Raider voiced his opinion of Tuz's business practices, one of the pirate's [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] attacked the pilot. As Naeco and Farlander moved to help their friend, Tuz brought a halt to the altercation and admonished his bodyguard's behavior before explaining that he was working for the Alliance as part of an arrangement with the ''Independence''{{'s}} commanding [[Officer/Legends|officer]], [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]]. On another occasion, Naeco suggested taking [[Flight Cadet]] [[Breth Gart]] to [[Lucky Lower Thirteen]], a [[Cantina/Legends|bar]] aboard the ''Independence'', in an effort to help him to integrate with his wingmates. The pilots soon attracted two female crew members, one of whom was clearly interested in Gart. When the young pilot decided to follow Farlander's lead in retiring for the night, the women stayed in the company of Naeco and Raider.<ref name="XW:OSG" />

===Battle of Yavin===
{{Quote|Red Twelve, right behind you, Red Leader.|Puck Naeco|<ref name="ANH-radio">[[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]]</ref>}}
[[File:Xwings_trenchrun.png|thumb|right|230px|Naeco and Nett navigate the Death Star trench.]]
The Empire soon completed construction of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] and dispatched it to destroy the Alliance's [[Great Temple/Legends|base]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].<ref name="ANH" /> The ''Independence'' traveled to the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]] to assist in the preparations for the imminent attack and Naeco was one of several pilots transferred to Yavin Base upon arrival to bolster its starfighter squadrons.<ref name="TEGW" /><ref name="XW:OSG" /> The stolen Death Star plans revealed a weakness in the battlestation: a small [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] leading to the main [[Reactor/Legends|reactor core]]. With the Death Star's defenses geared towards defending the station from a large-scale attack, the Rebels believed it would be possible for their starfighters to navigate down a narrow trench on the Death Star's surface, and fire [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] into the exhaust port, triggering a chain reaction that would destroy the station.<ref name="ANH" /> Naeco was assigned an X-wing as part of Red Squadron during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], one of two squadrons responsible for attacking the exhaust port. Flying with the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] [[Red Twelve/Legends|Red Twelve]],<ref name="TEGW" /> Naeco acted as wingmate to [[Red Leader/Legends|Red Leader]] [[Garven Dreis/Legends|Garven Dreis]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|88|Red Twelve}}</ref>

Following a briefing by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]], the Rebel pilots intercepted the Death Star as it prepared to use its [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] against Yavin 4. Dreis led Red Squadron in strafing runs against the battlestation's surface while three of [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadron's]] [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL Y-wing starfighters]] made an unsuccessful run on the exhaust port, resulting in the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of all three pilots. Red Squadron had already sustained losses, but Dreis regrouped the remaining fighters for an attack on the exhaust port. On Dodonna's instructions to split his group to allow two attempts, Dreis ordered [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]] and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to wait while he led Naeco and [[Theron Nett/Legends|Theron Nett]] in [[Red Ten/Legends|Red Ten]] into the trench. The three Rebels initially came under heavy [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] fire, but when the firing stopped, Dreis ordered his wingmates to watch for enemy fighters. Skywalker soon warned that a pair of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]], led by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]], was entering the trench behind them. Closing on the exhaust port, Dreis ordered Naeco and Nett to hold off the approaching [[TIE series/Legends|TIEs]] while he made his shot, but the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] soon closed the distance and fired on Naeco's X-wing,<ref name="ANH" /> causing it to explode and crash into the wall of the trench,<ref name="ANH junior">[[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' junior novelization]]</ref> killing the pilot.<ref name="TEGW" /> After Dreis and Nett were also killed by Vader's group, the three remaining members of Red Squadron attempted a trench run, with Skywalker finally succeeding in destroying the Death Star.<ref name="ANH" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Sorry Jan-lo. I guess I've been taken.|Puck Naeco, on finding himself kissing a Quarren|<ref name="XW:OSG" />}}
Naeco was a skilled pilot and [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]]. Although he could sometimes be reckless in combat, he was admired by his wingmates for his accurate deflection shooting<ref name="XW:OSG" /> and served as a mentor to younger pilots.<ref name="TEGW" /> He was popular with those with whom he worked, despite his habit for carrying out practical jokes at their expense. Examples of Naeco's jokes included tampering with his comrades' food in order to make their urine glow in the dark and playing a seductive female voice over the [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] while they engaged in [[Flight simulator/Legends|simulated]] combat practice. When members of Red Squadron used his attraction to Sunnar Jan-lo to turn the tables on him, he reacted with good humor but subsequently reduced the frequency of his jokes.<ref name="XW:OSG" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|When Red 10 gets shot down, the pilot we see die is someone else – a previously unseen male pilot with a helmet that looks like Janson's in ''The Empire Strikes Back''. That pilot, we decided, should be Red 12.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Notes">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/24614452839/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-10|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 10}}</ref>}}
Naeco was created by [[Rusel DeMaria]] for the [[1993]] book ''[[X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide]]'', which presented the story of Keyan Farlander, the player character in the [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]. In the book, Naeco is established as one of the previously unidentified members of Farlander's squadron. ''X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide'' established that several pilots from the ''Independence'' participated in the Battle of Yavin, but does not specifically name Naeco among them.<ref name="XW:OSG" /> However, ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' ([[2012]]) by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart|Paul Urquhart]] [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the character as Red Twelve, a pilot seen during the Battle of Yavin in [[George Lucas]]'s [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="TEGW" /><ref name="ANH" /> Red Twelve is not mentioned in dialog in ''A New Hope'' but is identified as one of Red Leader's wingmates during his unsuccessful trench run in the script<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> and in the [[Star Wars (radio)|radio drama adaptation]]. Red Twelve has a line of dialog in the ''Star Wars'' radio drama, but the credits do not identify which actor portrayed him.<ref name="ANH-radio" /> In the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novel]] and [[Star Wars (1977) 6|comic]] adaptations of ''A New Hope'', Red Squadron is called [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Blue Squadron]] and Naeco is referred to as Blue Twelve.<ref name="ANH-novel">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="SW6">[[Star Wars (1977) 6|''Star Wars'' (1977) 6]]</ref> Likewise, Red Squadron is called Gold Squadron in ''[[The Star Wars Storybook]]'', with Naeco referred to as Gold Twelve.<ref name="TSWS">''[[The Star Wars Storybook]]''</ref>

While writing ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Naeco was one of several characters considered as the identity of Red Twelve, along with Fin Danglot from ''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'' ([[1989]]), Milar Travis from [[Droids (1986) 8|''Droids'' (1986) 8]] ([[1987]]), [[Talos Merkin]] from ''[[Star Wars Journal: Captive to Evil]]'' ([[1998]]) and [[Ernek Marskan]] from ''X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide''. Travis was Fry's preferred option, due to his desire to include a female pilot among Red Squadron. However, in the film, when Theron Nett's starfighter is shot down moments after Red Twelve's, the pilot who is seen dying is not Nett. As a result, Fry and [[Leland Chee]], manager of the [[Holocron continuity database]], decided that this pilot should be Red Twelve, making the character male. Naeco was chosen from the remaining options while Travis and Danglot were both mentioned in Naeco's biography. Naeco's first name, which was never used in ''X-Wing: The Official Strategy Guide'', was also revealed in ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' as Puck, based on a suggestion by Chee.<ref name="Notes" />

Before ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' identified Red Twelve as Naeco, [[John Chapman]], who portrayed an unidentified Rebel pilot in ''A New Hope'', unofficially identified his character as Red Twelve, a Rebel pilot named Gil 'Drifter' Viray.<ref name="Cite web X-Wing">{{WebCite|url=http://www.red12.org|text=Homepage|work=[https://web.archive.org/web/20110923200329/http://www.red12.org X-Wing Pilot: Official Website of John Chapman, Red 12, Star Wars]|archivedate=20110923200329|nolive=1}}</ref> Since Naeco was identified as Red Twelve, another actor named [[Chris Matthews]] has also claimed the role, and has started to attend conventions.<ref name="Autograph">{{WebCite|url=http://planetdagobah.com/autographclassitrilogy.htm|text=Autograph Classic Trilogy|archivedate=20171115021856}}</ref>
